articleBlocks: At first, this looked more like materials and substances than the real category.
Lead pushed me in that direction immediately.
Iron kept that theory alive for a moment, but oxygen still did not quite fit.
That was the moment the first idea stopped working.
Then Oxygen made me stop thinking about materials and substances and start thinking about the real category.
Lead fit once I read it through the answer.
Iron fit once I read it through the answer.
The answer was Names of chemical elements.
Carbon and Oxygen then felt less surprising and more like the last pieces falling into place.
Looking back, the answer feels obvious in the best way.
solutionNarrative: I first read Lead and Iron too literally and drifted toward materials and substances. Lead could be read as "lead", while Iron could be read as "iron", so the board still felt open instead of solved.

Oxygen changed the direction because "oxygen" gave me a testable phrase, not just a loose topic. Once that line worked, I had a fixed place to put the repeated word and could go back through the earlier clues with a clearer target.

I then checked "lead", "iron", "silicon", and "carbon". Those checks mattered because each one landed as ordinary wording on its own, so I was not forcing five separate hints into one bag. The board started to behave like one phrase pattern across Lead, Iron, Silicon, Carbon, and Oxygen.

That left very little room for the earlier false start. The answer was "Names of chemical elements", and the last step was simply making sure every clue used that same reading cleanly before treating the solve as finished.
